cohort_definition: Undergraduate Summer Analysts in Evercore's advisory business (Strategic Advisory M&A and sector teams, Capital Markets Advisory, Private Capital Advisory & Fundraising, restructuring/liability management), penultimate-year students, and the full-time Analyst class they convert into. Equities, Wealth Management, and MBA Summer Associates are out of scope except where a posting is cited for cadence comparison.

compensation_notes.note: Official postings for 2027 New York advisory summer roles (Strategic Defense & Shareholder Advisory; Capital Markets Advisory) state an Expected Base Salary Range of $120,000–$120,000 — an annualized base figure printed on the posting under NY pay-transparency practice; the posting does not state how summer pay is prorated, and this record does not convert it.

For contrast within the same firm and cycle, the 2027 Wealth Management Summer Analyst posting states $80,000–$80,000 — compensation is division-specific; do not quote the advisory figure for other divisions.

entry_routes.details: Ten-week program; small teams, client contact, internal training program. Candidates apply to a specific group/office (e.g., M&A generalist or sector teams in New York, Houston, Chicago, Menlo Park/San Francisco, Toronto) rather than to a single central pool.
entry_routes.route: Strategic Advisory Summer Analyst (M&A and sector groups) — the main route

entry_routes.details: Distinct advisory tracks with their own postings: Private Funds Group (GP Advisory or LP Distribution verticals), Private Capital Markets and Debt Advisory, Liability Management & Restructuring, Strategic/Defense & Shareholder Advisory. Each counts toward the two-application limit in the 2028 cycle.
entry_routes.route: Specialist advisory tracks (Private Capital Advisory & Fundraising; Capital Markets Advisory; Restructuring)

entry_routes.details: Postings describe the summer as a representative analyst experience with accelerated responsibility versus bulge-bracket firms; a published conversion rate does not exist and none is stated.

hiring_bar_summary: Firm-published bar: pursuing an undergraduate degree graduating in the cohort window (Dec 2027–Jun 2028 for Summer 2027; Dec 2028–Jun 2029 for Summer 2028), all majors encouraged, strong academic record with diverse interests, demonstrated knowledge of investment banking and global markets, quantitative/analytical talent, and effective communication (official postings, verified 2026-10-12). Notably, Evercore publishes NO numeric GPA minimum on the postings reviewed — 'strong academic record' is the stated standard, so any specific Evercore GPA cutoff quoted elsewhere is unsourced. One specialist track (Strategic Defense & Shareholder Advisory) lists a Finance or Accounting major as preferred; the general M&A postings do not.

dated_windows.window: 2028 advisory cycle: applications open September 8, 2026, close November 15, 2026; NOT reviewed on a rolling basis; maximum two applications per student
2027 cycle (for comparison): some New York advisory postings ran a January 1 – February 1, 2026 window with rolling review and interviews

hiring_cadence.summary: Cadence changed between the two cycles on record — a freshness warning in itself. For Summer 2027, several New York advisory postings opened January 1, 2026 with a February 1, 2026 submission target and rolling review. For Summer 2028, the firm moved earlier and changed mechanics: applications September 8 – November 15, 2026, explicitly NOT reviewed on a rolling basis, with a strict maximum of two applications (a withdrawn application cannot be replaced). Always re-verify the current cycle's mechanics on evercore.com/careers; last cycle's rules do not carry over.

interview_styles.style: Technical depth is signaled by the work itself: postings name financial modeling and 'resolving complex accounting issues' as core summer tasks, so accounting/valuation fluency is the interview currency (agent reading of official posting content, labeled)

Reported norm for elite boutiques generally (not firm-published): heavy technical grilling plus 'why this firm / why boutique' fit, with small-team culture making partner-level exposure part of assessment. Label as community-reported.

known_biases_of_data: Built from the firm's official ATS postings and one university career-center relay of the firm's posting text; the ATS blocks automated readers, so posting text was verified via search-index crawls of the official URLs dated within a day of verification.
Cadence facts differ by cycle and by group; this record preserves both cycles rather than blending them, but a reader who skims may still apply the wrong cycle's rules.
No licensed population sample: school, major, and prior-employer distributions are omitted by design rather than estimated.
The two-application limit and non-rolling review are documented for the 2028 cycle; assuming they held in earlier cycles would be an error.

major_dist.note: Official postings say all majors are encouraged to apply for the general advisory tracks; one specialist track (Strategic Defense & Shareholder Advisory, 2027) lists Finance or Accounting as preferred. No major mix of actual hires is published.

path_patterns.pattern: Direct-to-group hiring: candidates pick specific group/office postings (M&A generalist, sector teams, or specialist advisory tracks) and, in the 2028 cycle, may hold at most two applications — so track selection is itself a strategic decision, unlike central-pool banks.
Ten-week summer on small teams with client and partner contact is the firm's stated analyst experience; the pitch is earlier responsibility than at bulge-bracket firms.

Reported norm (Doc 3 §4.1, labeled): boutique recruiting rewards direct networking into the specific group; with class sizes small, a warm introduction to the team applied to matters more than portal volume. Community-reported, not firm policy.

prior_employer_dist.note: Not published by the firm; omitted rather than estimated.

process_stages.stage: Application via evercore.com/careers during the published window; in the 2028 cycle applications are held and reviewed after the window rather than rolling
Interviews (in the 2027 cycle, postings state applications are reviewed and interviews occur on a rolling basis)
Ten-week summer program with a firm-run internal training program at the start, then desk work on live advisory assignments

red_flags: Cycle-mechanics trap: 2027 ran rolling with a Jan–Feb window; 2028 runs Sep–Nov, non-rolling, max two applications. Advice built on last cycle's rules (e.g., 'apply the day it opens, rolling') is wrong for 2028 — timing inside the window matters less than the two-application choice.
No GPA number is published; any 'Evercore requires a 3.7' claim is unsourced folklore.
Withdrawing an application does not free a slot in the 2028 cycle — a careless first application permanently burns one of two shots.
The $120,000 figure is an annualized base on the posting, not a summer paycheck figure; quoting it as summer pay would mislead.
referral_weight_notes: The firm publishes no referral policy for campus hiring. Reported norm (labeled): elite-boutique classes are small and group-specific, so partner/analyst relationships and school recruiting contacts are widely reported to matter; the documented process, however, is a capped two-application portal submission. Do not present referral weight as firm-stated.

school_dist.note: No school distribution is published by the firm for this cohort and no licensed population sample was available, so no distribution is stated.

screening_signals.signal: No numeric GPA cutoff published; 'strong academic record coupled with diverse interests' is the stated academic screen
'Demonstrated knowledge in investment banking and global markets' is a named qualification — prior finance exposure/technicals are part of the stated screen, not just potential
Graduation-window eligibility is a hard screen (Dec 2028–Jun 2029 for the Summer 2028 cohort)
Two-application cap (2028 cycle) functions as a self-selection screen: the firm forces focus on the two best-fit tracks

skills_dist.note: Skills are the postings' stated work content: financial modeling, complex accounting issue resolution, industry analysis, due diligence, client-meeting preparation, and (for Private Funds Group) LP/GP fundraising support and market mapping. Stated requirements, not measured frequencies among hires.

thesis_text: Bottom line: Evercore hires summer analysts directly into specific advisory groups on a ten-week program built around small teams and live deal work, and its recruiting mechanics just changed — for Summer 2028, applications run September 8 to November 15, 2026, are NOT reviewed on a rolling basis, and each student gets at most two applications, with no replacement if one is withdrawn (firm application instructions, verified 2026-10-12). Who gets in, per the firm's stated screen: penultimate-year undergraduates (graduating Dec 2028–Jun 2029 for the 2028 cohort), all majors welcome, with a strong academic record — the firm publishes no GPA number — plus demonstrated knowledge of investment banking and markets, quantitative talent, and communication skills. What the firm says vs. what to plan for: because review is batched and applications are capped, the highest-leverage decision is which two tracks to pick (M&A/sector groups vs. specialist tracks like Private Capital Advisory, Capital Markets Advisory, or Restructuring), not how fast you click submit. Routes in, ranked: (1) the two chosen group applications, each tailored to that group's deal type; (2) networking into the specific group ahead of the window — the reported boutique norm, and the only way to choose tracks intelligently; (3) the experience ladder underneath (smaller-bank or search-fund internships) that makes 'demonstrated knowledge' true on the resume. Compensation signal: New York advisory postings for 2027 carried a $120,000 expected annualized base salary range. Risks and alternatives: burning both applications on poor-fit tracks is the cycle's distinctive failure mode; bulge-bracket rolling programs are the hedge because their windows and mechanics differ. Offer to execute: map your two track choices against your experience, then draft group-specific applications.

values_culture_signals.signal: The firm's own framing is boutique: desire and flexibility to work in a boutique environment, learn on the job, work on several projects concurrently, and take responsibility earlier than at traditional bulge-bracket firms, with close partner contact
